title: Clifford inequality on a nodal curve with no separating node
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes with completed local $k$-algebras $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Cohomology means Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and $h^i(X,F)=\dim_k H^i(X,F)$. Assume that for every decomposition $X=A\cup B$ into two nonempty reduced unions of distinct irreducible components with no common component, the finite intersection $A\times_XB$ has $k$-length at least two (the condition is vacuous if $X$ is irreducible). The fibre product and its length mean [def-pc-fibre-product] and $\dim_k\Gamma(A\times_XB,\mathcal O_{A\times_XB})$. Let $M$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], with a section nonzero at every component generic point, and suppose there exists a map $M\to\omega_X$ nonzero at every component generic point, where $\omega_X$ is [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch]. Then
$$h^0(X,M)\leq \tfrac12\deg_k M+1,$$
with Euler-characteristic degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Irreducible components have the meaning of [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Section 2, Theorem 2.7 (Cartier subcanonical case), printed pp.40--41, and Section 4 Proposition 4.1 proof, printed p.48, two-connected case; replace the injective map by its Cartier zero divisor and use Riemann--Roch. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness; $X$ is Noetherian, and its invertible modules are coherent. Fix the given map $\varphi:M\to\omega_X$. On an affine open trivializing both lines it is multiplication by $f$. Every minimal-prime image of $f$ is nonzero. If $fa=0$, its image in each corresponding domain gives $a=0$ there; reducedness says the intersection of the minimal primes is zero, hence $a=0$. Thus $\varphi$ is injective and its local image ideal $(f)$ is Cartier. Write $T$ for the zero scheme: $M=I_T\otimes\omega_X$ inside $\omega_X$. It contains no component, hence is zero-dimensional. The given section of $M$ shows $T$ is subcanonical. Set $\ell=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $r=r(T)$. The splitting-index definition applies to this actual subspace of canonical sections.

source.place: Tags 02OR (lemma-zero-scheme), 0AYL (lemma-regular-section-associated-points); elementary reduced-ring injectivity argument written explicitly

proof.text: Apply the base-ideal lemma to $L=M$ and its full section space $V$. It gives $\mathcal B$, $b\ge0$ and $\bar T$ with $\ell(\bar T)=\ell+b$ and the same canonical section subspace $V$. Thus $\bar T$ is subcanonical and $r(\bar T)=r$, since admissible partitions use only that subspace and its component supports. If $r=0$, then $b\ge r$. If $r>0$, choose an admissible partition into $r+1$ blocks realizing $r$. Each block and its complement are nonempty. By the hypothesis each boundary contains at least two nodes. Each node between blocks is counted twice in the sum of the block boundaries, so $|E_{\mathcal P}|\ge r+1$. The base-ideal lemma gives $b\ge |E_{\mathcal P}|\ge r+1\ge r$. Self-nodes within a block are not counted.

source.place: Theorem 3.9 proof, printed p.247: base-locus correction; boundary count specialized to nodes

proof.text:
Use the splitting-corrected inequality for $\bar T$. With $p_a=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, the preceding equalities and $b\ge r$ give
$$h^0(X,M)=h^0(X,I_{\bar T}\otimes\omega_X)\le p_a-\frac{\ell+b}{2}+\frac r2\le p_a-\frac\ell2.$$
This is the cancellation of the splitting correction; no Cartier assumption on $\bar T$ is needed.

source.place: Theorem 3.9 proof, printed p.247, final inequality using Theorem 3.7

proof.text:
The defining exact sequence is $0\to M\to\omega_X\to\omega_X\otimes\mathcal O_T\to0$. Euler additivity and the zero-dimensional-support tensor formula give $\chi(X,M)=\chi(X,\omega_X)-\ell$. Reduced-curve duality gives $\chi(X,\omega_X)=-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and the definition of Euler-characteristic degree gives
$$\deg_kM=-2\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)-\ell=2p_a-2-\ell.$$
Substitution into step 3 yields $h^0(X,M)\le\deg_kM/2+1$. This also covers $T=\varnothing$ and irreducible $X$.
